title: ANCE or ENCE?
kidRule: A-N-C-E and E-N-C-E sound just the same, so there is no sure rule and each word has to be remembered. A handy tip: word cousins keep the same vowel, so a word with a cousin ending in A-N-T (like distant) usually takes A-N-C-E, and a cousin ending in E-N-T (like different) usually takes E-N-C-E.
hint: The ending sounds like 'unss', but its vowel is hiding. Do you know a cousin of this word that ends in 'unt'? It can help you choose the vowel.
reminder: This 'unss' ending has two spellings: A-N-C-E and E-N-C-E. If your first try did not work, try the other one!

check.question: Why do we have to remember that BALANCE ends with A-N-C-E?
check.correctAnswer: Because A-N-C-E and E-N-C-E sound the same, so listening can't tell us which one to use!
distractors: Because A-N-C-E is used in every word that has a B
Because E-N-C-E is only for very short words

words.def: The skill of staying steady without falling over.
words.sent: The gymnast kept her balance on the narrow beam.
words.story: Tiny tubes filled with liquid deep inside your ears help you keep your balance!
words.card: The seal kept its *balance* on a giant basket*bal*l!

words.def: Learning about the world by watching closely, asking questions, and doing tests.
words.sent: In science we made a volcano that fizzed.
words.story: The word comes from a Latin word that means 'knowledge'!
words.card: In *science* class my *sci*ssors learned to dance!

words.def: The door or opening where you go into a place.
words.sent: We met at the entrance to the zoo.
words.story: Beavers build the entrance to their home underwater so that enemies cannot get in!
words.card: A hippo *ran* through the *entrance* and got stuck like a cork!

words.def: The way that two things are not the same.
words.sent: Can you spot the difference between the two drawings?
words.story: One difference between an alligator and a crocodile is the snout: an alligator's is wide like a U, and a crocodile's is pointy like a V!
words.card: What a *difference* it would make *if* fish wore tiny shoes!

words.def: A special van with a siren that rushes sick or hurt people to get help.
words.sent: The ambulance raced by with its lights flashing.
words.story: The word is often painted backwards on the front of the van, so drivers ahead can read it the right way in their mirrors!
words.card: I *am* driving an *ambulance* for teddy bears with tummy aches!

words.def: The people who watch or listen to a show.
words.sent: The audience clapped when the puppets bowed.
words.story: The word is a cousin of 'audio', because both come from a Latin word that means 'to hear'!
words.card: The *audience* of penguins began to appl*aud* with their flippers!

words.sent: Our teacher talked about the importance of washing our hands.
words.story: Doctors learned the importance of washing their hands in the 1800s, when a doctor named Ignaz Semmelweis showed that it saved lives!
words.card: The captain knew the *importance* of parking his rubber duck in the right *port*!

words.def: A show, like a play, a dance, or a concert, that people do for others to watch.
words.sent: Our class gave a performance of a funny play.
words.story: The lyrebird of Australia gives an amazing performance: it can copy the sounds of other birds, and even camera clicks and chainsaws!
words.card: The flea circus gave a *performance* *for* one very itchy dog!

words.def: A time when someone or something is not there.
words.sent: The teacher noticed his absence from class.
words.story: Outer space has an absence of air, which is why astronauts need space suits and why there is no sound out there!
words.card: During the cat's *absence*, the mice did sit-ups to build their *abs*!

words.def: Something that happens to you, or what you learn from doing things.
words.sent: Riding a horse was a new experience for me.
words.story: An elephant herd is led by its oldest female, because her many years of experience help her remember where to find water!
words.card: The *exper*t pancake flipper has years of *experience* and one pancake stuck on the ceiling!
